safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a history of eczema.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No past medical history of eczema is included in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting a history of eczema (atopy) has minimal impact in an acute suspected sting-related allergic reaction, as it typically does not change immediate emergency management. At most it provides minor context for allergic predisposition.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a history of aerosinusitis.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No history of aerosinusitis is included in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Aerosinusitis history is unlikely to affect assessment or urgent treatment decisions for acute breathing difficulty after an apparent sting. The omission is therefore clinically negligible in this scenario.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No penicillin allergy is documented in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document a penicillin allergy is high-risk because it can directly lead to prescribing a contraindicated antibiotic and precipitate an allergic reaction, potentially including anaphylaxis. Medication allergy omissions are inherently dangerous even if not immediately relevant to this encounter.
